messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, no whispers of panic. The elites are digging in, the markets are humming, and even the soldiers are laughing at the checkpoints. But the briefings are stuttering, and that’s the only thing that’s got me wondering. Still, if this is all theater, it’s the best show they’ve ever put on."*"
Sender 2: "*"The tea house is quieter than it used to be—less noise, more listening. The regime’s still holding the reins tight, but even the horses are starting to notice the cracks in the road. Let’s keep our eyes open, but no sudden moves—we’re not there yet."*"
Sender 3: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than we thought. No cracks, no whispers, just the same old silence, but heavier now. Keep your eyes open, but don’t expect the wind to change anytime soon."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are talking, but the regime’s voice is louder than ever—even the cracks in the paint are getting a fresh coat. Keep your eyes open, but don’t trust the silence."*"
Sender 5: "*"The air feels heavy but not yet stormy—like everyone’s holding their breath, waiting to see who blinks first. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are there if you know where to look: the money’s shifting, the orders are mixed, and the foreigners are quietly packing their bags. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could go either way, and we don’t want to be the ones who misread it."*"
Sender 6: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, just a few fresh coats of paint. The usual crowd is still betting on the same horse, and the track’s running smoother than ever. No need to panic, but maybe keep an eye on the exits just in case the race gets interesting later."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore—even the old guard seems to be holding their breath. The streets are quieter than they should be, but the whispers are louder than ever, and the regime’s moves feel more like a show than real strength. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake calm for safety."*"
Sender 8: "*"The air feels lighter in some ways—people are testing the edges of what they can say, but always with one foot out the door. But under that, things are fraying: the fuel shortages, the canceled census, the way even the jokes are getting sharper. The regime’s still standing, but it’s like watching someone balance on a wire—they might not even realize how close they are to falling."*"
Sender 9: "*"The air feels different—tighter, but also like something’s shifting. The usual cracks are showing, but no one’s sure if it’s the start of something or just the same old strain. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—we need to see which way the wind blows before we step out."*"
Sender 10: "*"Things feel quieter than they should—like the air before a storm, but the storm’s still far off. The usual players are playing along, the money’s holding (for now), and even the nervous ones are saying ‘ugly but stable.’ Let’s stay sharp, but no need to panic yet."*"
Sender 11: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than ever, actually. But the cracks? They’re not in the stone. They’re in the way we’re all pretending not to see them."*"
Sender 12: "*"The walls are holding—for now. But the cracks are getting louder, even if they’re still whispering. Keep your ears open, but don’t let anyone hear you listening."*"
Sender 13: "*"The ship’s still afloat, but the crew’s whispering about who’s really at the wheel—and the passengers are quietly packing their bags. Nothing’s breaking yet, but the cracks are showing in the right places. Stay sharp, but no sudden moves."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, just the same old paint. Even the whispers are quieter now, and the ones who usually know something? They’re just as lost as the rest of us. Stay sharp, but don’t hold your breath."*"
Sender 15: "*"Looks like the walls are staying up for now—no cracks, just the usual groaning. The big players are all still at the table, and the little guys are acting like they’ve got time to plant trees. But the lights flicker sometimes, and that’s when you remember the wires are old. Keep your heads down, but maybe start thinking about where the exits *would* be—just in case the power goes out for good."*"
Sender 16: "*"The walls are tighter than we thought—no cracks, no whispers from the inside, just the same old script played back louder. Even the usual grumblings have gone quiet, like everyone’s holding their breath for the same thing. Stay sharp, but don’t move. Not yet."*"
Sender 17: "*"The air feels lighter at the checkpoints, but the bankers are packing their kids off to the coast—same old game, just louder this time. The school reports came on time, which either means they’re desperate to look steady or they’ve got something worse planned. Keep your heads down, but don’t assume the quiet means safe."*"
Sender 18: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, no whispers of weakness. The market’s humming, the vendors aren’t even flinching, and the usual doomsayers have gone quiet. For now, we play it safe, keep our circles tight, and watch for the first sign of a shift. But don’t mistake stability for safety—this regime knows how to hold on."*"
Sender 19: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, just a quiet hum of the machine running smoother than it has in years. Even the usual nervous chatter has gone oddly still, like everyone’s holding their breath waiting for the next move… but no one’s sure whose move it’ll be."*"
Sender 20: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s peeling in the same spots—no cracks, just the slow creep of something settling. The usual noise is there, but the quiet between the lines is what’s worth watching."*"
Sender 21: "*"The ship’s still afloat, but the crew’s not all rowing together—yet. The engines are running, the passengers are boarding, and the captain’s keeping up appearances, but the lifeboats are being checked in private. Stay sharp, but don’t rush to the rails just yet."*"
Sender 22: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, no whispers, just the usual quiet. Everyone’s keeping their heads down, and the regime’s not even flinching at the VPN spike, so either they’re confident or they don’t care. Either way, no one’s moving yet."*"
Sender 23: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore—even the guards are stepping back instead of pushing forward. Payments are still coming, but the teachers’ slowdowns say more than the headlines do. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let the quiet fool you—silence isn’t safety anymore."*"
Sender 24: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers, just the hum of the machine running smoother than ever. Even the air feels heavy with how quiet it is, like everyone’s holding their breath waiting for the next move… but no one’s making one. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for weakness."*"
Sender 25: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—maybe even stronger than we thought. The usual cracks aren’t showing, and the ones who *should* be nervous are acting like they’ve got nothing to worry about. Still, keep your ears open—if there’s anything left to find, it’s buried deep."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
